([[Kansas City, Missouri]]) | college = [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] (2018–2022) | highlights = * [[NCAA champion]] ([[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022]]) * [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|NCAA Final Four Most Outstanding Player]] (2022) * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2022]]) * [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] (2022) * First-team All-[[Big 12]] (2022) }} '''Ochai Young Agbaji''' (born April 20, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). As a senior at the [[University of Kansas]], Agbaji was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and voted the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] in 2022. He led the Jayhawks to a national championship and was named the [[NCAA Division I basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four Most Outstanding Player]] (MOP). Agbaji was drafted as the 14th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA Draft|2022 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. However, he was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in September before playing a regular-season game in [[Cleveland]]. He was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 2024. ==Early life== Agbaji was born in [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin]], but grew up mainly in [[Kansas City, Missouri]].{{cite web |last=Tait |first=Matt |title=Ochai Agbaji's father, Olofu, explains his son's 'special purpose' after 95–68 Kansas win vs. Milwaukee |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2019/dec/11/ochai-agbajis-father-olofu-explains-his-sons-speci/ |website=KUSports.com |access-date=January 25, 2022 |date=December 11, 2019}} He grew up playing [[soccer]], upon his father's encouragement, playing club soccer as well as [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball from a young age. Agbaji stopped playing soccer as a sophomore at [[Oak Park High School (Kansas City, Missouri)|Oak Park High School]] in [[Kansas City, Missouri]] to focus on basketball. He grew {{Convert|9|in|cm|spell=in}} between his freshman and junior years.{{cite web |last=Mellinger |first=Sam |title=How and why Kansas freshman Ochai Agbaji went from overlooked recruit to NBA prospect |url=https://www.kansascity.com/latest-news/article226565829.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=November 19, 2019 |date=February 21, 2019}} In his basketball career at Oak Park, Agbaji did not receive offers from any [[Power Five conferences|Power Five]] college programs until his senior season. As a senior, he averaged 27.6 points and 8.6 rebounds per game for Oak Park and was named ''[[Kansas City Star]]'' All-Metro player of the year.{{cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |last2=McDowell |first2=Sam |title=It's official: Oak Park senior Ochai Agbaji signs with Kansas basketball |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article208641889.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=November 19, 2019 |date=April 11, 2018}} Agbaji was considered a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite web |last=Skretta |first=Dave |title=Jayhawks' Agbaji is proof that big-time talent still sneaks under recruiting radar |url=https://www.foxsports.com/kansas-city/story/kansas-jayhawks-ochai-agbaji-is-proof-that-big-time-talent-still-sneaks-under-recruiting-radar-022519 |website=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 19, 2019 |date=February 25, 2019}} On February 8, 2018, he committed to play college basketball for [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] over offers from [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] and [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].{{cite web |last=Daniels |first=Evan |title=Ochai Agbaji commits to Kansas |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Ochai-Agbaji-commits-to-Kansas-114883729/ |website=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=November 19, 2019 |date=February 8, 2018}} ==College career== Agbaji began his freshman season at the [[University of Kansas]] as a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] and was a member of the [[Practice squad|scout team]].{{cite web |last=Moore |first=CJ |date=January 10, 2019 |title=Redshirt burned, Ochai Agbaji comes up big for Kansas |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/759792/2019/01/10/redshirt-burned-ochai-agbaji-comes-up-big-for-kansas/ |access-date=December 21, 2024 |website=nytimes.com |via=[[The Athletic]]}} In early January 2019, his redshirt was lifted because [[2018–19 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] needed depth after [[Udoka Azubuike]] suffered a season-ending injury and [[Silvio De Sousa]] faced eligibility issues.{{cite web |last=Chasen |first=Scott |title=Ochai Agbaji to burn redshirt, play Bill Self announces |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/Article/Ochai-Agbaji-to-burn-redshirt-play-Bill-Self-announces-on-Hawk-Talk-127548387/ |website=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=November 19, 2019 |date=January 8, 2019}} On January 29, Agbaji made his first career start, scoring 24 points, bringing in seven rebounds, and stealing the ball twice in a loss to [[2018–19 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]]. In his next game, he recorded his first [[double-double]] in a win over [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]]. Agbaji was named [[Big 12 Conference]] Newcomer of the Week for the two performances.{{cite web |title=Agbaji named Big 12 Newcomer of the Week |url=https://kuathletics.com/mens-basketball-agbaji-named-big-12-newcomer-of-the-week/ |publisher=Kansas Jayhawks |access-date=November 19, 2019 |date=February 4, 2019 |archive-date=February 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200219080900/https://kuathletics.com/mens-basketball-agbaji-named-big-12-newcomer-of-the-week/ |url-status=dead }} Agbaji averaged 8.5 points and 4.6 rebounds per game in 22 games, including 16 starts as a freshman.{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |title=Agbaji's rapid rise gives KU scoring threat: 'He is poised to have a bust-out year' |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article236894623.html |access-date=November 23, 2019 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |date=November 1, 2019}} On November 5, 2019, Agbaji made his sophomore season debut, scoring 15 points in a loss to fourth-ranked [[2019–20 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] at the [[Champions Classic]].{{cite web |date=November 5, 2019 |title=No. 3 Kansas upended by No. 4 Duke, 68–66 |url=https://kuathletics.com/news/2019/11/5/no-3-kansas-upended-by-no-4-duke-68-66 |access-date=December 21, 2024 |publisher=Kansas Jayhawks}} During the aforementioned sophomore season, Agbaji was named Honorable Mention All-Big 12.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced |url=https://big12sports.com/documents/2020/3/8//All_Big_12_Release_19_20_.pdf |website=[[Big 12 Conference]] |access-date=March 8, 2020 |date=March 8, 2020}} As a sophomore, Agbaji averaged 10 points and 4.2 rebounds per game and finished second on the team with 46 three-pointers.{{cite news |last=Braswell |first=Scott |title=Azubuike named Big 12 Player of the Year |url=http://www.kten.com/story/41868018/azubuike-named-big-12-player-of-the-year |access-date=April 4, 2020 |work=KTEN |date=March 8, 2020}} He averaged 14.1 points per game as a junior, shooting 42 percent from the field. On April 8, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Gates |first=Riley |title=Ochai Agbaji declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Kansas-Jayhawks-basketball-Ochai-Agbaji-declares-for-2021-NBA-Draft-Bill-Self-163878833/ |website=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=May 30, 2021 |date=April 8, 2021}} Agbaji made his senior season debut on November 9, 2021, recording 29 points in an 87–74 win against [[2021–22 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] at the Champions Classic.{{cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |title='He's a pro': Ochai Agbaji scores career-high 29 as KU Jayhawks beat Michigan State |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article255659641.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=November 15, 2021 |date=November 10, 2021}} On January 24, 2022, he scored a career-high 37 points in a 94–91 double-overtime win over [[2021–22 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]].{{cite news |title=Agbaji helps No. 5 Kansas beat Texas Tech 94–91 in 2OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401368387 |access-date=January 25, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 25, 2022}} At the close of the season, Agbaji was voted the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] and was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].{{cite press release|url= https://big12sports.com/news/2022/3/6/mens-basketball-all-big-12-awards-announced.aspx |title= Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced |publisher=[[Big 12 Conference]] |date=March 6, 2022 |access-date=March 6, 2022}} Kansas won the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]], and he scored 12 points in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game]] and was named the [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|tournament MOP]].{{cite news|first=Gary|last=Bedore|title=Kansas Jayhawks' Ochai Agbaji adds NCAA Tournament MOP to All-America, Big 12 awards|date=April 4, 2022|newspaper=The State|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/ncaa/article260105450.html|access-date=April 5, 2022}} On April 24, Agbaji declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |date=April 24, 2022 |title=Kansas guard Ochai Agbaji declares for 2022 NBA draft, says 'I'll always be a Jayhawk' |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33800854 |access-date=April 24, 2022 |website=ESPN}} ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2022–2024)=== Agbaji was selected with the 14th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |last=Salaam |first=Tayo |date=June 24, 2022 |title=Nigerians In NBA Draft: Agbaji Picked By Cavaliers, Williams Headed To Charlotte |url=https://www.channelstv.com/2022/06/24/nigerians-in-nba-draft-agbaji-picked-by-cavaliers-williams-headed-to-charlotte/ |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=Channels Television}}{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Jonathan |date=2022-06-24 |title=What do you think of the Cavs taking Ochai Agbaji at No. 14? |url=https://cleveland.com/sports/2022/06/what-do-you-think-of-the-cavs-taking-ochai-agbaji-at-no-14.html |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=cleveland.com}} On July 2, 2022, Agbaji signed his rookie scale contract with the Cavaliers.{{Cite web |date=July 2, 2022 |title=Cavaliers Sign 2022 Draft Picks Ochai Agbaji and Isaiah Mobley |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-2022-draft-signings-220702 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On September 1, 2022, Agbaji was traded, alongside [[Collin Sexton]], [[Lauri Markkanen]], three first-round picks and two pick swaps, to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Donovan Mitchell]].{{cite web |date=September 3, 2022 |title=Cavs Acquire Three-Time All-Star Donovan Mitchell |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-mitchell-trade-220903 |access-date=3 September 2022 |website=NBA.com}} Agbaji had his NBA debut on October 19, playing one minute in a 123–102 win over the [[2022–23 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web |last=Coles |first=Matthew |date=October 20, 2022 |title=NEW-LOOK JAZZ BEAT NUGGETS 123-102 IN SEASON OPENER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200012 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On April 8, 2023, Agbaji scored a career-high 28 points in a 118–114 win over the Nuggets.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202304080UTA.html|title=Nuggets vs Jazz, April 8, 2023|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} ===Toronto Raptors (2024–2026)=== On February 8, 2024, Agbaji was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] alongside [[Kelly Olynyk]] in exchange for [[Kira Lewis Jr.]], [[Otto Porter Jr.]], and a [[2024 NBA draft|2024]] first-round draft pick, which became the 29th selection.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS ACQUIRE OLYNYK AND AGBAJI FROM JAZZ|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-acquire-olynyk-and-agbaji-from-jazz|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} He made 27 appearances (18 starts) for Toronto over the remainder of the season, averaging 6.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Ochai Agbaji 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4397018/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=April 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On November 27, 2024, Agbaji scored a game-high 24 points on 9-of-10 shooting and made 6-of-7 three-pointers in a 119–93 win against the [[2024–25 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]]. He made 64 total appearances (including 45 starts) for Toronto during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], logging averages of 10.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 1.5 assists (all of which where career-highs).{{Cite web|title=Ochai Agbaji 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4397018/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=April 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Agbaji played in 42 games (making 13 starts) for the Raptors during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 4.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 0.7 assists.{{Cite web|title=Ochai Agbaji 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4397018/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=April 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2026)=== On February 5, 2026, Agbaji was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] that sent [[Chris Paul]] to the Raptors.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-acquire-ochai-agbaji-in-three-team-trade|title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Ochai Agbaji in Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2026}} ==Career
